evidence: Inspected full 10-line helper; only scans settled results and throws a fixed TRPCError; no retained payload or allocation concern.

Inspected full 290 lines and callers in docker-router.ts plus Docker reconciliation UI. Per-container matching scans apps/integrations and creates candidate projections; inventory and DB collections are functionally required for reconciliation. No workload cardinality evidence supports an actionable complexity finding.

Inspected full 302 lines, registered router and UI/widget callers. Container target input is capped at 100; logs tail capped at 1000; log subscription cleanup marks inactive and invokes stream cleanup. No actionable memory issue established.

Inspected full 451 lines and management/access-picker callers. Paginated list caps through shared paginatedSchema; getAll is used for admin group management and maps member relation rows to required user display fields. No actionable finding established.

Inspected full 196 lines and registry/context callers. Registry intentionally retains one client per configured context; context probes run two requests per context with a 5-second timeout. No config-size/cardinality measurement establishes a concrete retained-memory issue.
Inspected full 17 lines and all assigned router use; retrieves a context client and translates only not-found errors, with no material allocation.
Inspected full 61 lines and MCP registration. Router modules are dynamically imported inside procedures; only contexts, ingresses and pods are exposed. No eager import finding.
Inspected full 41 lines; parser instances are request-local and do scalar conversion. No actionable allocation.
Inspected full 69 lines; parser lookup tables are instance fields but parser instances are short-lived and used in node loops. Tiny fixed tables do not establish an actionable retained-memory issue.
Inspected full 3-line interface; no runtime behavior.
Inspected full 2-line scalar helper; no material allocation beyond formatting one percentage.

Full 219-line inspection. getClusterResourceCounts concurrently obtains eight full Kubernetes lists and only returns each items.length (lines 159-178); dashboard invokes it on mount alongside getCluster, which independently fetches all pods (cluster-dashboard.tsx lines 25-34; cluster.ts lines 24-28). See report F1.

Inspected full 35 lines and admin page/table caller. Full ConfigMap objects are mapped to name/namespace/time, so payload overfetch exists but no observed size or data-volume evidence distinguishes it from required inventory retrieval; dashboard count finding is recorded under cluster.ts.
Inspected full 17 lines and Kubernetes context selector/server caller; returns the compact status projection produced by concurrent bounded probes.

Inspected full 60 lines and admin page/table/MCP callers. It maps full ingress responses into displayed names, class, host/path/backend and timestamp. No response-size measurement supports a separate finding.
Inspected full 16 lines and root/MCP registration; each Kubernetes subrouter is lazily imported.
Inspected full 35 lines and admin page/table caller; maps namespace records to displayed phase/name/time; no concrete scale evidence for a separate issue.
Inspected full 77 lines and server/client table callers. Fetches nodes and node metrics, projects displayed fields; metric lookup is linear per node but node/metric cardinality evidence is absent.

Full 113-line inspection and admin SSR/client table callers. In the per-pod loop, ReplicaSet ownership is fetched with await (lines 33-52); each call constructs an AppsV1Api and reads the same namespace/name without memoization (lines 77-103). See report F2.

Inspected full 35 lines and admin page/table caller. Inventory maps name/namespace/type/time and never returns secret data; it still receives full secret objects. The directly measured use of the same full secret list solely for a count is captured in F1.
Inspected full 39 lines and admin page/table caller; maps service fields used by the table, with no concrete scale evidence for separate optimization.
Inspected full 41 lines and admin page/table caller; maps PVC fields displayed by the table, with no concrete scale evidence for separate optimization.

Full 128-line inspection and shared upload widget callers. uploadMedia converts every uploaded File to an ArrayBuffer concurrently and retains all buffers until the bulk DB insert completes (lines 59-76). Schema caps each file at 32 MiB, while nginx allows 256 MiB per request and there is no aggregate file-count/size cap (validation/media.ts lines 8-35; nginx.conf line 26). See report F3.
Inspected full 169 lines and package query helpers. Settings are small typed values; board validation selects only IDs; no large allocation or retained collection.

Dedicated full-file pass in four contiguous ranges (lines 1-240, 241-480, 481-720, 721-924), plus user management, user picker and profile-layout callers. List/selectable outputs include images used by avatars; 350,000-character profile image cap exists but no user-count/image-size measurements establish a separate actionable finding. Preference routes delegate to the inspected preferences module.
Inspected full 103 lines and user router callers. Reads only selected preference columns; patch validates merged header state and writes one row. No actionable memory issue.
